facts.name: Cinnamon Fern
facts.light: Part shade to sun; likes wet to moist soil
facts.notes: A bold fern with fuzzy cinnamon-colored spikes in spring. Best in damp spots and slow to spread.

companions.why: Combines well with astilbe, columbine and ferns; plant with wild ginger, Virginia bluebells, Jacob's ladder and wild geranium; mix with iris.

companions.why: Combines well with hosta and ferns; eye-catching near dark-leaved Heuchera, Pulmonaria or Brunnera; a backdrop for dark astilbe.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Japanese Forest Grass article

companions.why: Contrasts nicely with vertical perennials such as iris, liatris, ferns and salvia.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Lady's Mantle article

companions.why: Combine with astilbe, ligularia and ferns in shade; fine foliage contrasts with hostas.
Combines well with bleeding hearts, ferns, lungworts, bergenia, wild ginger, astilbes and hostas.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Solomon's Seal article

companions.why: Combines well with anemone, astilbe, ferns, hellebores, hosta and lungwort.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Toad Lily article

companions.why: Hostas and ferns both work well as companions; use other plants to hide gaps after it goes dormant.

companions.why: Goes well with Jack-in-the-pulpit; combine with hosta, astilbe, bleeding heart, columbine, hellebore, heuchera, lungwort and ferns.

companions.why: Found with Solomon's seal, ferns, mayapple and woodland phlox; combines with celandine poppy, columbine, foamflower and goat's beard.
